title: The hypertrophy series: diffuse vs targeted tonnage
summary: He distinguishes lifts that spread tonnage across the body (deadlift) from those that target one muscle (lateral raise). Programs need both compounds and isolation to cover every body part, and diffuse tonnage must be tracked to avoid overuse injuries.
claims: Some lifts diffuse tonnage across the body, like the deadlift, while others target it to a few muscles, like the lateral raise
Picture each lift as a heat map of where tonnage goes; knowing which muscles a lift works is essential to programming
The deadlift's targeted tonnage goes to hamstrings, glutes and lower back while the upper back only gets diffuse tonnage, so it cannot be your only upper back builder
Traps are called an enhanced-only muscle because people rely on deadlifts, where traps only get a weighted stretch; traps can hold far more than your deadlift and need more tonnage
Compounds diffuse tonnage, save time, pre-fatigue and warm up; isolation movements are special agents delivering targeted tonnage
Big-three-only training leaves you with an unaesthetic body, while isolation-only bros stay small and weak and can never catch up in tonnage
Size is driven by overall tonnage
Go through every body part when choosing exercises to make sure each is covered, noting the diffuse tonnage each lift adds
Ignoring diffuse tonnage causes overuse injuries, such as the lower back taxed by both squats and deadlifts, and tendons worn by the same joint angles
